tier_description: Adversarial & Edge Cases — questions with false assumptions, hidden conflicts, or policy violations that a naive system would miss; correct response requires identifying and explaining why the student's premise or plan fails

pattern_descriptions.A: Impossible Timeline (5 questions) — student requests something that cannot be completed given scheduling, prereq chains, or AW unit caps
pattern_descriptions.B: Hidden Prerequisite Violation (5 questions) — shallow prereq check passes but a deeper transitive requirement is unmet
pattern_descriptions.C: Policy Conflict (5 questions) — student's plan violates a policy (overload, P/N, double-counting) they are unaware of
pattern_descriptions.D: Course Availability Trap (5 questions) — course exists in catalog but is not offered in the target semester
pattern_descriptions.E: Double-Counting / Requirement Ambiguity (5 questions) — student attempts to count one course toward two requirements where policy disallows it
pattern_descriptions.F: False Premise (5 questions) — student's question contains a factual error the system must identify and correct

schema.pattern: A/B/C/D/E/F — the adversarial pattern this question exemplifies
schema.persona_id: Persona identifier (always present for T5 questions)
schema.persona_summary: One-line description of the student's situation
schema.question: Natural-language question containing a trap, false assumption, or hidden conflict
schema.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: What the student believes vs. what is actually true or permissible
schema.naive_system_response: What a less careful advising system would incorrectly say
schema.correct_response: What the system should actually say, identifying the conflict/error
schema.domains_required: List of domains needed to detect the trap
schema.why_multi_agent_helps: How a multi-agent architecture reduces the risk of falling into this trap
schema.key_facts: Critical facts that must be retrieved to answer correctly
schema.known_traps: Specific pitfalls that make this question hard
schema.advisor_validation_needed: Items requiring human advisor sign-off before acting on the answer

quality_notes: All 30 questions have an identifiable trap that causes naive systems to fail
All 6 patterns have exactly 5 questions each
All 30 questions are persona-grounded using 29 distinct personas
naive_system_response documents the wrong answer for contrast with the correct one
known_traps field explicitly names the pitfalls for use in failure-mode analysis
Answers require advisor validation before deployment
why_multi_agent_helps field supports architectural analysis of the advising system
